NKJV.1: Now it came to pass after these things that God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
NKJV.2: Then He said, “Take now your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I shall tell you.”
NKJV.3: So Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son; and he split the wood for the burnt offering, and arose and went to the place of which God had told him.
NKJV.4: Then on the third day Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the place afar off.
NKJV.5: And Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey; the lad and I will go yonder and worship, and we will come back to you.”
NKJV.6: So Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife, and the two of them went together.
NKJV.7: But Isaac spoke to Abraham his father and said, “My father!” And he said, “Here I am, my son.” Then he said, “Look, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
NKJV.8: And Abraham said, “My son, God will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering.” So the two of them went together.
NKJV.9: Then they came to the place of which God had told him. And Abraham built an altar there and placed the wood in order; and he bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar, upon the wood.
NKJV.10: And Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.
NKJV.11: But the Angel of the LORD called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” So he said, “Here I am.”
NKJV.12: And He said, “Do not lay your hand on the lad, or do anything to him; for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from Me.”
NKJV.13: Then Abraham lifted his eyes and looked, and there behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. So Abraham went and took the ram, and offered it up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
NKJV.14: And Abraham called the name of the place, The-LORD-Will-Provide; as it is said to this day, “In the Mount of the LORD it shall be provided.”
NKJV.15: Then the Angel of the LORD called to Abraham a second time out of heaven,
NKJV.16: and said: “By Myself I have sworn, says the LORD, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son—
NKJV.17: blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your descendants as the stars of the heaven and as the sand which is on the seashore; and your descendants shall possess the gate of their enemies.
NKJV.18: In your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
NKJV.19: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose and went together to Beersheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beersheba.
NKJV.20: Now it came to pass after these things that it was told Abraham, saying, “Indeed Milcah also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
NKJV.21: Huz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
NKJV.22: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
NKJV.23: And Bethuel begot Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
NKJV.24: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Thahash, and Maachah.

ESV.1: After these things God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
ESV.2: He said, “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I shall tell you.”
ESV.3: So Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and his son Isaac. And he cut the wood for the burnt offering and arose and went to the place of which God had told him.
ESV.4: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar.
ESV.5: Then Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey; I and the boy  will go over there and worship and come again to you.”
ESV.6: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. And he took in his hand the fire and the knife. So they went both of them together.
ESV.7: And Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” And he said, “Here I am, my son.” He said, “Behold, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
ESV.8: Abraham said, “God will provide for himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they went both of them together.
ESV.9: When they came to the place of which God had told him, Abraham built the altar there and laid the wood in order and bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
ESV.10: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
ESV.11: But the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
ESV.12: He said, “Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
ESV.13: And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, behind him was a ram, caught in a thicket by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son.
ESV.14: So Abraham called the name of that place, “The LORD will provide”;  as it is said to this day, “On the mount of the LORD it shall be provided.”
ESV.15: And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham a second time from heaven
ESV.16: and said, “By myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son,
ESV.17: I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and as the sand that is on the seashore. And your offspring shall possess the gate of his  enemies,
ESV.18: and in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice.”
ESV.19: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they arose and went together to Beersheba. And Abraham lived at Beersheba.
ESV.20: Now after these things it was told to Abraham, “Behold, Milcah also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
ESV.21: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
ESV.22: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
ESV.23: (Bethuel fathered Rebekah.) These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
ESV.24: Moreover, his concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

CSB17.1: After these things God tested Abraham <sup>ⓑ</sup> and said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he answered.
CSB17.2: “Take your son,” he said, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, <sup>ⓒ</sup> go to the land of Moriah, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I will tell you about.”
CSB17.3: So Abraham got up early in the morning, <sup>ⓔ</sup> saddled his donkey, and took with him two of his young men and his son Isaac. He split wood for a burnt offering and set out to go to the place God had told him about.
CSB17.4: On the third day <sup>ⓕ</sup> Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
CSB17.5: Then Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there to worship; then we’ll come back to you.”
CSB17.6: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac. <sup>ⓖ</sup> In his hand he took the fire and the knife, <sup>ⓗ</sup> and the two of them walked on together.
CSB17.7: Then Isaac spoke to his father Abraham and said, “My father.” And he replied, “Here I am, my son.” Isaac said, “The fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
CSB17.8: Abraham answered, “God himself will provide <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” Then the two of them walked on together.
CSB17.9: When they arrived at the place that God had told him about, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac <sup>[2]</sup> and placed him on the altar <sup>ⓙ</sup> on top of the wood.
CSB17.10: Then Abraham reached out and took the knife to slaughter his son.
CSB17.11: But the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He replied, “Here I am.”
CSB17.12: Then he said, “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.13: Abraham looked up and saw a ram <sup>[3]</sup> caught in the thicket by its horns. So Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
CSB17.14: And Abraham named that place The LORD Will Provide, <sup>[4]</sup> so today it is said: “It will be provided <sup>[5]</sup> on the LORD’s mountain.”
CSB17.15: Then the angel of the LORD called to Abraham a second time from heaven
CSB17.16: and said, “By myself I have sworn,” <sup>ⓛ</sup> this is the LORD’s declaration: “Because you have done this thing and have not withheld your only son,
CSB17.17: I will indeed bless you <sup>ⓜ</sup> and make your offspring as numerous as the stars of the sky <sup>ⓝ</sup> and the sand on the seashore. <sup>ⓐ</sup> Your offspring will possess the city gates of their enemies. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.18: And all the nations of the earth will be blessed <sup>[6]</sup> by your offspring <sup>ⓒ</sup> because you have obeyed my command.”
CSB17.19: Abraham went back to his young men, and they got up and went together to Beer-sheba. And Abraham settled in Beer-sheba.
CSB17.20: Now after these things Abraham was told, “Milcah also has borne sons to your brother Nahor: <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.21: Uz his firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel the father of Aram,
CSB17.22: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
CSB17.23: And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Milcah bore these eight to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
CSB17.24: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

AMP.1: Now after these things, God tested [the faith and commitment of] Abraham and said to him, "Abraham!" And he answered, "Here I am."
AMP.2: God said, "Take now your son, your only son [of promise], whom you love, Isaac, and go to the region of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I shall tell you."
AMP.3: So Abraham got up early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him and his son Isaac; and he split the wood for the burnt offering, and then he got up and went to the place of which God had told him.
AMP.4: On the third day [of travel] Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
AMP.5: Abraham said to his servants, "Settle down and stay here with the donkey; the young man and I will go over there and worship [God], and we will come back to you."
AMP.6: Then Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on [the shoulders of] Isaac his son, and he took the fire (firepot) in his own hand and the [sacrificial] knife; and the two of them walked on together.
AMP.7: And Isaac said to Abraham, "My father!" And he said, "Here I am, my son." Isaac said, "Look, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
AMP.8: Abraham said, "My son, God will provide for Himself a lamb for the burnt offering." So the two walked on together.
AMP.9: When they came to the place of which God had told him, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood, and bound Isaac his son and placed him on the altar, on top of the wood.
AMP.10: Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to kill his son.
AMP.11: But the Angel of the LORD called to him from heaven and said, "Abraham, Abraham!" He answered, "Here I am."
AMP.12: The LORD said, "Do not reach out [with the knife in] your hand against the boy, and do nothing to [harm] him; for now I know that you fear God [with reverence and profound respect], since you have not withheld from Me your son, your only son [of promise]."
AMP.13: Then Abraham looked up and glanced around, and behold, behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up for a burnt offering (ascending sacrifice) instead of his son.
AMP.14: So Abraham named that place The LORD Will Provide. And it is said to this day, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen and provided."
AMP.15: The Angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time
AMP.16: and said, "By Myself (on the basis of Who I Am) I have sworn [an oath], declares the LORD, that since you have done this thing and have not withheld [from Me] your son, your only son [of promise],
AMP.17: indeed I will greatly bless you, and I will greatly multiply your descendants like the stars of the heavens and like the sand on the seashore; and your seed shall possess the gate of their enemies [as conquerors].
AMP.18: Through your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have heard and obeyed My voice."
AMP.19: So Abraham returned to his servants, and they got up and went with him to Beersheba; and Abraham settled in Beersheba.
AMP.20: Now after these things Abraham was told, "Milcah has borne children to your brother Nahor:
AMP.21: Uz the firstborn and Buz his brother and Kemuel the father of Aram,
AMP.22: Chesed and Hazo and Pildash and Jidlaph and Bethuel."
AMP.23: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight [children] Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
AMP.24: Nahor's concubine, whose name was Reumah, gave birth to Tebah and Gaham and Tahash and Maacah.

WEB.7: Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am, my son.” He said, “Here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
WEB.8: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.
WEB.9: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.
WEB.10: Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.
WEB.11: Yahweh’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
WEB.12: He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
WEB.13: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
WEB.14: Abraham called the name of that place Yahweh Will Provide.  As it is said to this day, “On Yahweh’s mountain, it will be provided.”
WEB.15: Yahweh’s angel called to Abraham a second time out of the sky,
WEB.16: and said, “I have sworn by myself, says Yahweh, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son,
WEB.17: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring  greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring  will possess the gate of his enemies.
WEB.18: All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring,  because you have obeyed my voice.”
WEB.19: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
WEB.20: After these things, Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
WEB.21: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
WEB.22: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
WEB.23: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
WEB.24: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

NLT.1: Some time later, God tested Abraham’s faith. “Abraham!” God called. “Yes,” he replied. “Here I am.”
NLT.2: “Take your son, your only son — yes, Isaac, whom you love so much — and go to the land of Moriah. Go and sacrifice him as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”
NLT.3: The next morning Abraham got up early. He saddled his donkey and took two of his servants with him, along with his son, Isaac. Then he chopped wood for a fire for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had told him about.
NLT.4: On the third day of their journey, Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
NLT.5: “Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told the servants. “The boy and I will travel a little farther. We will worship there, and then we will come right back.”
NLT.6: So Abraham placed the wood for the burnt offering on Isaac’s shoulders, while he himself carried the fire and the knife. As the two of them walked on together,
NLT.7: Isaac turned to Abraham and said, “Father?” “Yes, my son?” Abraham replied. “We have the fire and the wood,” the boy said, “but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
NLT.8: “God will provide a sheep for the burnt offering, my son,” Abraham answered. And they both walked on together.
NLT.9: When they arrived at the place where God had told him to go, Abraham built an altar and arranged the wood on it. Then he tied his son, Isaac, and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.
NLT.10: And Abraham picked up the knife to kill his son as a sacrifice.
NLT.11: At that moment the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Yes,” Abraham replied. “Here I am!”
NLT.12: “Don’t lay a hand on the boy!” the angel said. “Do not hurt him in any way, for now I know that you truly fear God. You have not withheld from me even your son, your only son.”
NLT.13: Then Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. So he took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
NLT.14: Abraham named the place Yahweh-Yireh (which means “the LORD will provide”). To this day, people still use that name as a proverb: “On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
NLT.15: Then the angel of the LORD called again to Abraham from heaven.
NLT.16: “This is what the LORD says: Because you have obeyed me and have not withheld even your son, your only son, I swear by my own name that
NLT.17: I will certainly bless you. I will multiply your descendants beyond number, like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will conquer the cities of their enemies.
NLT.18: And through your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed — all because you have obeyed me.”
NLT.19: Then they returned to the servants and traveled back to Beersheba, where Abraham continued to live.
NLT.20: Soon after this, Abraham heard that Milcah, his brother Nahor’s wife, had borne Nahor eight sons.
NLT.21: The oldest was named Uz, the next oldest was Buz, followed by Kemuel (the ancestor of the Arameans),
NLT.22: Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
NLT.23: (Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.) In addition to these eight sons from Milcah,
NLT.24: Nahor had four other children from his concubine Reumah. Their names were Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

NET.1: Some time after these things God tested Abraham. He said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am!” Abraham replied.
NET.2: God said, “Take your son — your only son, whom you love, Isaac — and go to the land of Moriah! Offer him up there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will indicate to you.”
NET.3: Early in the morning Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took two of his young servants with him, along with his son Isaac. When he had cut the wood for the burnt offering, he started out for the place God had spoken to him about.
NET.4: On the third day Abraham caught sight of the place in the distance.
NET.5: So he said to his servants, “You two stay here with the donkey while the boy and I go up there. We will worship and then return to you.”
NET.6: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on his son Isaac. Then he took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them walked on together.
NET.7: Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father?” “What is it, my son?” he replied. “Here is the fire and the wood,” Isaac said, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
NET.8: “God will provide for himself the lamb for the burnt offering, my son,” Abraham replied. The two of them continued on together.
NET.9: When they came to the place God had told him about, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood on it. Next he tied up his son Isaac and placed him on the altar on top of the wood.

NET.11: But the LORD’s angel called to him from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.

NET.13: Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram caught in the bushes by its horns. So he went over and got the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son.

NET.16: and said, “‘I solemnly swear by my own name,’ decrees the LORD, ‘that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son,

NET.21: Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram),

NET.23: (Now Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.) These were the eight sons Milcah bore to Abraham’s brother Nahor.
